lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Elizabeth opens by showing she has understood his words all along.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert admits he sometimes shortened visits just to reach the moment of taking her hand.

lines.text: How I wish for two hearts to love you with, and two lives to give to you, and two souls to bear the weight worthily of all you have given to me.
lines.note: Elizabeth wishes for two hearts and two lives to give him.

lines.text: I love you, I think, perceptibly more in these latter days!
lines.note: Robert says he loves her perceptibly more in these latter days.

lines.text: Here is a distress for me, dearest!
lines.note: Elizabeth writes in distress that poor Flush has been stolen.

lines.text: Poor Flush—how sorry I am for you, my Ba!
lines.note: Robert answers with immediate sympathy for Flush and for Elizabeth.

lines.text: Was ever any in the world, in any possible world, so perfectly good and dear to another as you are to me!
lines.note: Elizabeth marvels at how perfectly good and dear he is to her.

lines.text: Dearest, you are a prophet, I suppose—there can be no denying it.
lines.note: Elizabeth calls him a prophet when family plans suddenly threaten delay.

lines.text: Words can never tell you, however,—form them, transform them anyway,—how perfectly dear you are to me—perfectly dear to my heart and soul.
lines.note: Robert says words can never tell how perfectly dear she is to him.

lines.text: My own beloved, if ever you should have reason to complain of me in things voluntary and possible, all other women would have a right to tread me underfoot, I should be so vile and utterly unworthy.
lines.note: Elizabeth answers his wish to be better to her by saying he already lifted her into life.

lines.text: Bless you, my very own, only Ba—my pride, and joy, and utter comfort.
lines.note: Robert calls her his very own, only Ba, his pride, joy, and utter comfort.

lines.text: By to-morrow at this time, I shall have you only, to love me—my beloved!
lines.note: Elizabeth looks ahead to having him only, to love her, by the next day.
